title: An air-hockey puck keeps gliding when the air lifts it
summary: On an air-hockey table, air lifts the puck so friction nearly vanishes and the puck glides with little change in speed.
body: OpenStax Physics contrasts an air-hockey table with the air off and with the air on. With the air off, the puck slides only a short way before friction stops it. With the air on, the puck is lifted slightly, friction is very small, and the puck glides with very little change in speed. The page says that on a frictionless surface the net outside force would be zero, ignoring air resistance. Urone and Hinrichs, 26 March 2020. A real table is only nearly free of friction.
